> **In short:** Your brand voice stays safe when you (1) write the rules down on one page, (2) paste them into every AI chat, (3) test the output against your "don't" list, (4) keep a named human reviewing every draft, and (5) audit what company data you actually paste in. This guide walks through each step.

# How to Protect Your Brand's Voice in the Age of AI

Your brand voice is the personality that runs through every customer email, social post, and report. When AI starts drafting content for you, that personality can flatten fast — or worse, sensitive details can leak into prompts. The fix isn't avoiding AI. It's giving the AI clear rules and keeping a human in the loop. Here are five steps that work.

## Before you start

You will need:

- An AI chat tool you already use (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar)
- A place to save a short voice guide (a Google Doc, Word file, or Notion page works fine)
- About 30 minutes the first time through

No paid plan is required. The whole guide runs on free tiers.

## Step 1 — Write down your brand voice on one page

Open a blank document and write four short sections: **Tone** (friendly, formal, playful?), **Audience** (who reads this?), **Do** (3-5 example sentences you love), and **Don't** (3-5 phrases you never use, like "synergy" or "move the needle"). Keep it under one page — long guides don't get read.

💬 Paste this starter into your doc and edit it:
> *"Tone: warm but not gushy. Audience: small business owners, 30-55. Do: short sentences, second person, contractions. Don't: exclamation marks in formal emails, the word 'unlock,' the phrase 'game changer.'"*

**You'll know it worked when** a colleague who has never worked with your brand can read the page and write a paragraph that sounds like you.

## Step 2 — Turn the guide into a reusable AI prompt

Take the four sections and paste them as one block at the start of any AI conversation. Most AI chat tools also let you save instructions that apply to every chat — for example, ChatGPT's **Custom Instructions** field under settings, or the **Project Instructions** area when you open a new project in Claude.

💬 Copy-paste starter for the AI's system prompt:
> *"Follow these rules for every response. Tone: warm but not gushy. Audience: small business owners. Write in second person, short sentences. Never use 'unlock,' 'seamless,' or exclamation marks. Match the style of this sample: [paste 2-3 sentences from your existing content]."*

**You'll know it worked when** the AI's first reply already sounds closer to your brand than a blank-prompt reply would.

## Step 3 — Test the AI against your "Don't" list

Send the AI three real tasks: a customer email, a social post, and a short report intro. Then check each reply against your Don't list. Flag every banned phrase, every sentence that sounds generic, and every tone mismatch. If the AI keeps slipping, add more examples — showing usually beats telling.

💬 Test prompt to copy:
> *"Write a 100-word welcome email for a new customer. Then list every word in your draft that might break our brand guide, and why."*

**You'll know it worked when** the AI either avoids your banned phrases on its own or self-corrects them in the second pass.

## Step 4 — Add a human review before anything goes live

Decide who reads AI drafts before they ship. For emails and social posts, a quick 60-second scan is enough. For longer pieces (reports, blog posts, ad copy), add a second reviewer. Write the rule down: **no AI-generated text is published without one named human approving it.**

💬 Paste-this review checklist into your project tool:
> *"1. Does the tone match our voice guide? 2. Any banned phrases? 3. Any facts or numbers I didn't verify? 4. Anything that sounds generic or off-brand?"*

**You'll know it worked when** every published piece has a real person's name attached to it, not just "AI generated this."

## Step 5 — Audit what company data you actually paste into AI

Open your last five AI conversations and ask: did I paste anything sensitive? Common slips include unreleased product names, financial numbers, customer lists, or internal strategy docs. Make a short list of "never paste" items (your top three is fine) and keep it next to your voice guide.

💬 Paste this reminder near your AI login:
> *"Never paste into AI chats: unreleased product names, revenue or forecast numbers, customer email addresses, internal strategy memos."*

**You'll know it worked when** you can scroll through a week of AI chats and not find a single item from your "never share" list.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake:** Writing a 10-page voice guide and never using it. **Fix:** Keep it under one page. The AI reads it every chat; you should be able to read it in 90 seconds.
- **Mistake:** Letting AI publish without a human sign-off because the draft "looks fine." **Fix:** Even 60 seconds of review catches tone drift and hallucinations (when AI confidently makes something up). One named human, every time.
- **Mistake:** Pasting internal strategy docs into AI for "context." **Fix:** Give the AI your voice guide and high-level goals. Keep forecasts, customer lists, and unreleased product info out of the chat.
- **Mistake:** Editing AI drafts in your head instead of on the page. **Fix:** Always edit in writing. "Looks okay" is not the same as actually reading for banned phrases and wrong facts.

## What this means for you

- **If you're running a small business:** Start with Step 1 and Step 2 — they are the highest-impact. A one-page voice guide pasted into your AI tool fixes most tone drift in about 30 minutes.
- **If you're in marketing or communications:** Build Steps 4 and 5 into your team's workflow now. The voice guide only protects you if a human actually reviews the draft before it ships.
- **If you're just getting started with AI:** Don't skip Step 3. Testing the AI against your Don't list on day one shows you where it slips, before bad habits calcify.
